title: Jimmy Rochelle's territory band and Milt Buckner
summary: In Danville and Bass Lake he played in Rochelle's dance band with Bernie Peacock, where pianist Milt Buckner became like an older brother.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Yeah. No, we never did that (tour). And then I went to Danville, Illinois, and joined Jimmy Rochelle's band, which was a Territory band, and Bernie Peacock was with us. And then I met A. K. Atkinson, he was working in a road house in that town, along with Clark Terry. And Jimmy Rochelle had a Territory band. He sang a little song and we played dance music and we played arrangements and the main influence was Milt Buckner on piano. He was like an older brother to me and I learned a lot from him. And we worked around Danville and then we went up to Bass Lake, Michigan, and did a whole summer. And that's when I really got to know Milt Buckner and he was like an older brother to me. And that was quite an experience. And then when we got back together in Europe in '75 (sic)
and we reminisced about all that, 'cause we did a six month tour there. But that was two great experiences for me. And Bernie Peacock was a very fine alto player and he was a real friend. Yeah.
So between when you played with Milt Buckner in Jimmy Rochelle's band and when you played with him in Europe did you play with him in any...

Yeah, I did a couple of things with him at Birdland. Yeah, umhum. And he played with Hamp for many years. He was a fine arranger and played...you know he created the lock-hand style piano...which George Shearing incorporated, you know. And then he played marvelous vibes. He was a tremendous musician, yeah. I learned a lot from him.
